w: Today, a continuous chanting of the Swaminarayan Mahamantra was organised in the mandir from 6.00 a.m. From the city’s 48 areas, devotees from 39 areas chanted the Swaminarayan mantra while they walked together to the mandir.

After puja, while Swamishri was returning to his residence by car, Swamishri saw the devotees chanting the dhun. Swamishri had his car stopped and he stepped out and started clapping and chanting the dhun. The devotees were overwhelmed with joy. Swamishri asked for the microphone and began chanting the dhun for the next five minutes.
( See Special Report )

At 6.30 pm, Swamishri departed from Dubai International Airport and landed in Bahrain after a one hour flight. Swamishri was welcomed by Dr. Prafulbhai Vaidya, Jasbirsingh, Vinay Diwan and other devotees.

The Best of Devotees A few verses from the biography of Bhagwan Swaminarayan - 'Haricharitramrut Sagar' by Adharanand Swami - were read before Swamishri: "There is no greater sinner among devotees than one who speaks ill of another devotee. He is the best of devotees who sees his own faults." On hearing this verse a devotee remarked, "Bapa, this is very difficult to avoid. We see faults in others and not in our ownselves." Swamishri replied, "Because we fail to see our faults it has been so instructed. When you find fault in someone then you should introspect whether you've got it yourself. Someone may have lust whereas you may have greed. Someone may have jealousy whereas you may have ego. Our faults are written on our back whereas we see others' on their chest ..." "But Swamishri, it is only through divine grace that one can overcome this," a devotee added. "Yes. Only through grace can one realize this. That is why it has been said, 'Hari krupa jab hovat he, tab sujat apna dosh' (Only through God's grace can one see one's own faults). When we do 'seva' to please the Guru only, only then does one's base nature dissolves ..."
Riches bring fame but it increases the inclinations of faultfinding, enmity and ego.
By slowly bringing garbage in a clean home, the entire house will become full. Similarly, by looking at faults in others one will become full of faults.

To cater to students of higher secondary level from grade 8 to 12, the BAPS has planned to build an educational complex on the outskirts of Nagpur city. Swamishri performed the bhumi-pujan rituals by sprinkling kum kum, rice grains and flowers amidst Vedic chantings. Thereafter Swamishri sanctified the land by sprinkling flowers.
After his morning puja Swamishri performed the pujan rituals of murtis for the Kutir Mandir in Vaghamba (S. Gujarat).

ds.t: You leave even your own home
w: A young man came for darshan. He said, "My addictions will not leave me."
Swamishri said, "If you have to go to London or America, do you leave your home here or not?"
"Yes."
"Even though the home is your own, you leave it?"
"Yes."
Swamishri said, "We leave even what is our own, so this has come from outside; how long can it take to leave it? Give it up."

ds.t: Working in a bar without drinking
w: A young man named Kaushikbhai Modi said to Swamishri, "Until now I had done nothing but addictions, but on coming into contact with you, every addiction left me. My friends are amazed too. In fact my job is in a bar, so I have to serve people alcohol, but even there, by your grace, I do not feel like it. After the Chandkheda centenary festival, everything changed. Since then many temptations have come, but I have not drunk at all."

Tonight Swamishri was returning to his residence after casting his glance on the water show. It was about 8:40. Darkness had fallen. Swamishri was coming towards his residence in his wheelchair. In the Akshardham complex, lights were on only where needed. Even though the doors of Akshardham were closed, Swamishri bowed and did darshan as he passed.
As the wheelchair moved along, Swamishri asked Dharmakunvar Swami from Bhadra, one of the sadhus walking quickly behind, "How are the preparations for the pratishtha going?"
Dharmakunvar Swami told him everything, from the lodging to the building of the mandir and the renovation of the old mandir. In five minutes Swamishri got the whole picture of the preparations.
Swamishri's wheelchair was moving, with the light of a mobile tube light and the beam of a torch falling ahead. Even at such a time Swamishri made use of the time.

ds.t: We only fulfil Yogiji Maharaj's resolves
w: Once the sadhus were all sitting before Swamishri and talking. During the conversation Yagnesh Swami said, "What are your resolves?"
Swamishri said, "All the resolves Yogiji Maharaj made cannot even be completed, so why should we make separate ones? We are only trying to fulfil his resolves."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Never mind other resolves, but come, make one resolve."

Swamishri said, "There is none. We fulfil the resolves Yogiji Maharaj made; how many more should we make? Yogiji Maharaj spoke of colouring the universe, of growing satsang, of more sadhus. We go on within those resolves of his."
Narayancharan Swami said, "Your resolves are Yogiji Maharaj's resolves! So whatever you make would be called Yogiji Maharaj's!"
Laughing, Swamishri said, "You are the ones who think they are separate. Where do we think so?"
Vishwavihari Swami said, "Come, make one resolve: that you will stay on this earth another 100 years to fulfil Yogiji Maharaj's resolves."
Dharmavatsal Swami said, "Why a hundred? A hundred and twenty five."
Laughing, Swamishri said, "Why even a hundred and twenty five? Say more!"
Yagnesh Swami said, "We will say more, but our resolve is that you travel in this very same body."
Swamishri said, "Has that (body) ever stayed for anyone? Believe only that we are the soul."
Narayancharan Swami said, "But please keep it."

Swamishri said, "He (Yogiji Maharaj) will keep it. We depend on God. The work gets done through Him. Nothing happens by us. If one keeps saying 'I do, I do', one is finished. If pride comes, 'I did this, I did that', it is over. But if one lives as the soul, then honour, insult or scorn, nothing troubles."
Once the talk turned to Bhagatji Maharaj.

Swamishri said, "Just like Nachiketa, Bhagatji Maharaj asked Gunatitanand Swami only for knowledge of the soul. Even bearing suffering, he asked for knowledge of the soul. When Gunatitanand Swami told Bhagatji Maharaj, 'Ask for a boon,' and even offered temptations, Bhagatji Maharaj said only, 'If you are pleased, give me the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam.' That (Nachiketa's) story is from long ago, from the Vedic age, but these lived only recently. Shastriji Maharaj too served Bhagatji Maharaj. We speak only of the manifest, but 'I know how to swim and how to dive, but I forget my presence of mind.'"
Saying this, Swamishri said, "Isn't that right, Pandit?"
Shrutiprakash Swami said, "We forget. Because of our natures and faults we forget everything, so the joy of the soul and God lessens."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Caught up in honour and insult, we miss out on the joy of God."
Swamishri said, "Where is there any question of honour and insult? For one who has become brahmarup, how can all this get in the way?"

Saying this, Swamishri began to sing: "'Oneness in honour and insult, evenness in happiness and sorrow; yes sir, good sadhu...' Yogiji Maharaj used to sing this kirtan a lot. 'This happened to me, that happened to me, I got this, I did not get that', none of that happens at all. There is only oneness in honour and insult. If honour comes, it is God's grace, and if insult comes, it is God's wish. Whether sorrow comes or happiness, nothing happens except by His wish. With such thinking, sorrow never comes and there is no regret."
